'''Mohamadreza Baghaban Eslaminejad''' ({{langx|fa|محمدرضا باغبان اسلامی نژاد}}, born May 24, 1967, [[Tabriz]], [[Iran]]) is the director of the Adult Stem Cell Lab and [[histology]]/[[embryology]] Professor at the [[Royan Institute]] where he held a multi-departmental professorship in [[bioengineering]], [[tissue engineering]], [[regenerative medicine]], and [[stem cell therapy]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mohammad R. Baghban Eslaminejad Ph.D. {{!}}|url=http://royanstemcell.ir/mohamadreza-baghaban-eslaminejad/|website=www.royanstemcell.ir/|language=en-US|access-date=2020-12-07}}</ref> Eslaminejad studies have been cited over 4000 times.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=359N6-sAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Mohammad R. Baghban Eslaminejad - Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.com|access-date=2020-12-07}}</ref> He is best known for Hard Tissue Engineering ([[bone]], [[cartilage]], [[tooth]]) and utilizing [[Mesenchymal stem cells]] for treatment of orthopedic diseases.

He has researched numerous [[model organism]]s such as mouse, rabbit, and dog, issued in about 400 papers in international journals and conferences. Furthermore, he has contributed to more than 20 international books by writing the chapter and has written three national books.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://isid.research.ac.ir/Mohamadreza_BaghabanEslaminejad|title=Mohammad R. Baghban Eslaminejad - SID Research|website=isid.research.ac.ir|access-date=2020-12-08}}</ref> His leading research is focused on the advanced stages of the [[Clinical trial]] for utilizing [[Stem cell]] to treat patients. Prof. Baghaban Eslaminejad has won numerous [[Award]]s and serves as the [[Editorial Board]] of the Current Stem Cell Research and Therapy and the World Journal of Stem Cells.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://benthamscience.com/journals/current-stem-cell-research-and-therapy/editorial-board/|title=Current Stem Cell Research & Therapy - Editorial Board Members|website=benthamscience.com|access-date=2020-12-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wjgnet.com/1948-0210/editorialboard.htm|title=World Journal of Stem Cells - Editorial Board Members|website=www.wjgnet.com|access-date=2020-12-08}}</ref>

==Background and personal life==
Eslaminejad was born and grew up in [[Tabriz]], Iran. He then moved to [[Tehran]] in 1986. He graduated from [[Iran University of Medical Sciences]] in 1990 with a BSc in 
[[physical therapy]]. He received his MSc degree in [[anatomy]] from [[Tarbiat Modares University]] in 1997. His PhD was completed in Anatomical Sciences at Tarbiat Modares University in 2004, after attending a course of research in Center for Developmental Biology, [[Riken]], Kobe, [[Japan]] (2003-2004) then he instantly joined the stem cell department at the Royan Institute.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.royanstemcell.ir/?page_id=281|title= Royan Department of Stem Cells and Developmental Biology|website=www.royanstemcell.ir|access-date=2020-12-14}}</ref>

==Founder of stem cell lab==
In 2004, the Adult Stem Cell [[laboratory]] and its research group had been founded by Eslaminejad. This lab aimed to utilize stem cells, especially [[Mesenchymal stem cells]] (MSCs), to treat orthopedic diseases, especially bone and cartilage defects. Focusing on the therapeutic application of MSCs by Eslaminejad to regenerate bone and cartilage defect had made adult stem cells lab and its research group one of the main leading hard tissue engineering research group in Iran and made the world's attention.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2009/apr/15/iran-at-forefront-of-stem-cell-research/?page=all|title = The Washington Times: Iran at forefront of stem cell research|website=www.washingtontimes.com|access-date=2020-12-14}}</ref>

==Contributions to regenerative medicine==
Eslaminejad has considered the different aspects of hard tissue engineering. The majority of his research serves to accelerate the regeneration process in human bone/cartilage tissue. In the last five years alone, all of his international contributions have been published in reliable journals.<ref name="auto"/>

In 2015, his collaboration with [[Johannesburg]] Laser Research Center has highlighted the effect of [[Low-level laser therapy]] (LLLT) and [[Mesenchymal stem cells]] (MSCs) on bone regeneration. The histological analysis revealed a statistically meaningful increase in new bone formation.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Fekrazad | first1 = R | title=The effects of combined low level laser therapy and mesenchymal stem cells on bone regeneration in rabbit calvarial defects| journal=Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology B: Biology| date=October 2015| volume=151| pages=180–185| doi=10.1016/j.jphotobiol.2015.08.002 | pmid = 26298068 }}</ref>

His contribution with the [[University of Oxford]] in 2016 led to introduce the [[PLGA]] coated [[Tricalcium phosphate]] (β-TCP) scaffold as the desired substrate for bone tissue engineering, which expressed 
[[Type I collagen]] (COL1) and [[RUNX2]] significantly.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Khojasteh| first1 = A | title = Development of PLGA-coated β-TCP scaffolds containing VEGF for bone tissue engineering | journal = Materials Science and Engineering: C | date = December 2016 | volume = 69| pages = 780–788 | doi = 10.1016/j.msec.2016.07.011 | pmid = 27612772 | url = https://epublications.marquette.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1200&context=dentistry_fac | url-access = subscription }}</ref>

His interdisciplinary work in 2017 on hydrothermal treatment of [[Chitosan]] scaffolds manifested the novel nontoxic crosslinking method for cartilage tissue engineering.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Shamekhi | first1 = MA | title = Fabrication and characterization of hydrothermal cross-linked chitosan porous scaffolds for cartilage tissue engineering applications | journal = Materials Science and Engineering: C | date = November 2017 | volume = 80| pages = 232–242| doi = 10.1016/j.msec.2017.03.194 | pmid = 28866197 | doi-access = free }}</ref>

Another international collaboration with the [[University of Amsterdam]] illustrated the smart delivery capacity of VEGF-[[Poly(N-isopropylacrylamide)]] loaded collagen [[Hydrogel]] led to heightened angiogenic/osteogenic differentiation.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Adibfar | first1 = A | title = VEGF delivery by smart polymeric PNIPAM nanoparticles affects both osteogenic and angiogenic capacities of human bone marrow stem cells | journal = Materials Science and Engineering: C | date = December 2017 | volume = 93| pages = 790–799| doi = 10.1016/j.msec.2018.08.037 | pmid = 30274113 | s2cid = 52897461 }}</ref>

The multicenter research with [[Ali Khademhosseini]] and AO Research Institute Davos in [[Switzerland]] has also been established by Eslaminejad. The study was designed to targeted cell therapy of [[Osteoarthritis]] diseases to prevent off-target attachment of cells.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Nasiri| first1 = N | title = Targeted cell delivery for articular cartilage regeneration and osteoarthritis treatment | journal = Drug Discovery Today| date = November 2019 | volume = 24 | issue = 11 | pages = 2212–2224 | doi = 10.1016/j.drudis.2019.07.010 | pmid = 31398399 | s2cid = 199518365 }}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Eslaminejad's [[Interdisciplinarity]] investigation has been appreciated over 6 major national and international awards. In 2006, he received first prize in the seventh Royan International Research Award for Reproductive Biomedicine and Stem Cell.<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.royaninstitute.org/cmsen/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=162&Itemid=162|title = Royan International Research Award |website=www.royaninstitute.org|access-date=2020-12-14}}</ref> In 2007, he selected as The Leading Researcher of Tehran. In 2009, he received the best researcher award from Razi Medicine Festival in the Novel Technologies section, Tehran.<ref>{{Cite web|url =https://www.isna.ir/news/8710-01168/%DA%AF%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%B4-%D9%83%D8%A7%D9%85%D9%84-%D8%A8%D8%A7-%D8%AD%D8%B6%D9%88%D8%B1-%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%8A%D8%B3-%D8%AC%D9%85%D9%87%D9%88%D8%B1-%D8%A8%D8%B1%DA%AF%D8%B2%D9%8A%D8%AF%DA%AF%D8%A7%D9%86-%DA%86%D9%87%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%AF%D9%87%D9%85%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%AC%D8%B4%D9%86%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B1%D9%87|title = Razi Medicine Festival|website=www.isna.ir|access-date=2020-12-14}}</ref> In 2010, National Festival for Commemorating Distinguished Researchers was named Dr. Eslaminejad as the Excellent Researcher of Iran.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.farzaninstitute.com/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=1201|title = Excellent National Researcher|website=www.farzaninstitute.com|access-date=2020-12-14}}</ref> In 2015, he praised as the exemplary scientist and staff of the year by ACECR (The Academic Center for Education, Culture and Research). In 2018 and 2019, he was included in the list of scientific leaders of Iran and was praised.<ref>{{Cite web|url =http://217.146.218.138/webreport/view.action?webreport_code=9000&masterCode=49000079|title = Ellit National Researcher of 2018|website=217.146.218.138/homepage/homePage.action|access-date=2020-12-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url = http://res.royan.org/webdocument/load.action?webdocument_code=9000&masterCode=49000087|title = Ellit National Researcher of 2019|website=217.146.218.138/homepage/homePage.action|access-date=2020-12-14}}</ref>
Springer Nature selected one of the Eslaminejad chapter books with the title '3D Printing in Dentistry' as one of the 2020 highlighted research.<ref>{{Cite book|chapter-url = https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-21583-5_9|website= www.springernature.com/gp/researchers/campaigns/highlights|doi = 10.1007/978-3-030-21583-5_9| isbn=9783030215835 | s2cid=202780295 |access-date=2020-04-18 | chapter=3D Printing in Dentistry | title=Applications of Biomedical Engineering in Dentistry | date=2020 | last1=Hosseini | first1=Samaneh | last2=Halvaei | first2=Majid | last3=Ebrahimi | first3=Amin | last4=Shamekhi | first4=Mohammad Amin | last5=Baghaban Eslaminejad | first5=Mohamadreza | pages=195–221 }}</ref>
